assumptions: A finite number n of canonical bosonic modes and a positive trace-one density operator rho; all quadrature second moments are finite.
R is the ordered vector of Hermitian quadrature operators (q_1, p_1, ..., q_n, p_n); the same ordering is used for V and the canonical symplectic form Omega.
Expectations mean Tr(rho A), Delta R_i = R_i - <R_i>, and {A,B} = AB + BA; the formula uses symmetrized, centered moments.
No Gaussian-state assumption is needed. The first two moments determine the entire state only after a Gaussian-state assumption is supplied.
variables: V: finite 2n by 2n real symmetric covariance matrix; V_ii is Var(R_i).
R_i and R_j: canonical quadrature operators, not commuting phase-space coordinate values.
rho: the bosonic density operator; angle brackets: quantum expectation; i,j = 1,...,2n.
patches.regime: Exact second-moment definition for Gaussian and non-Gaussian states with finite second moments. It is not a full state description for a general non-Gaussian state and does not cover divergent-moment idealizations.
patches.units: V_ij has the product units of R_i and R_j. Fix [R_i,R_j] = i hbar Omega_ij in compatible quadrature units. The inspected review uses hbar = 2 and vacuum covariance I; dividing every quadrature by sqrt(2) gives hbar = 1 and vacuum covariance I/2, and divides V by 2.

assumptions: V_ij = (1/2)<{Delta R_i,Delta R_j}> is the finite real symmetric covariance of n canonical bosonic modes in a positive trace-one state.
The Hermitian quadratures obey [R_i,R_j] = i hbar Omega_ij, with hbar > 0 and Omega the real direct sum of n blocks [[0,1],[-1,0]], in the same ordering as V.
The inequality means positive semidefiniteness of the Hermitian matrix V + i(hbar/2)Omega, not entrywise nonnegativity.

Gaussianity is unnecessary for necessity. Conversely, a finite real symmetric V satisfying this condition is realizable as the covariance of a Gaussian state; the condition alone does not validate a proposed arbitrary non-Gaussian operator or Wigner function.
variables: V: symmetrized quadrature covariance; Omega: dimensionless canonical antisymmetric form.
hbar: positive commutator scale in the chosen compatible quadrature units; i: imaginary unit.
>= 0: Hermitian positive-semidefinite order, including equality at uncertainty saturation.
patches.regime: Exact covariance-level uncertainty relation for Gaussian and non-Gaussian physical states with finite second moments. For one mode it includes Var(q) Var(p) - Cov(q,p)^2 >= hbar^2/4. Covariance admissibility is not a complete characterization of general non-Gaussian states.
patches.units: The card restores arbitrary hbar to the inspected review equation V + i Omega >= 0, which uses [R_i,R_j] = 2i Omega_ij. For hbar = 1 the condition is V + i Omega/2 >= 0 and the vacuum has V = I/2; for hbar = 2 the vacuum has V = I.

assumptions: S is a finite 2n by 2n real matrix acting on a column vector of Hermitian quadrature operators R; n is a positive integer.
Omega is the nonsingular canonical form, the direct sum of n blocks [[0,1],[-1,0]], and R obeys [R_i,R_j] = i hbar Omega_ij.
The same quadrature ordering and normalization are used before and after the transformation; T denotes ordinary matrix transpose.
A real displacement d may be added in R -> SR + d without changing commutators. Gaussianity of the input state is not required for this algebraic condition.
variables: S: real linear transformation of 2n canonical quadratures; Omega: real canonical antisymmetric form.
S^T: ordinary transpose, not complex conjugate transpose; R: quadrature-operator column vector.
n: finite mode count; hbar: fixed commutator scale; d: optional real displacement vector.
patches.regime: Exact finite-mode canonical condition. Such transformations, with displacements, describe Gaussian unitaries; those unitaries can act on non-Gaussian inputs too. A general noisy Gaussian channel need not have a symplectic linear part and is not specified by this equation.
patches.units: S is expressed in a fixed compatible quadrature basis. The scalar hbar cancels from the commutator-preservation condition; a change of ordering must transform Omega at the same time. A rescaling between hbar = 2 and hbar = 1 is a convention change, not a symplectic map at fixed Omega and hbar.

assumptions: n is a finite positive integer and R is a real 2n-dimensional phase-space coordinate, not the operator vector appearing in the covariance definition.
The state is Gaussian, d is its real mean vector, and V is its finite real symmetric strictly positive-definite symmetrized covariance; V^(-1) and sqrt(det V) are well-defined.

To describe a quantum state, V must also satisfy V + i(hbar/2)Omega >= 0 in the declared canonical convention. Positive definiteness and a normalized Gaussian density alone do not ensure quantum physicality.
W is normalized with respect to the real quadrature measure d^(2n)R; changing to complex amplitudes or another scaled coordinate system requires the appropriate Jacobian.
variables: R: 2n real phase-space coordinates; d: mean quadrature vector; n: number of modes, so phase-space dimension is 2n.
V: symmetrized quadrature covariance in the same coordinates; det V: determinant; V^(-1): inverse.
W(R): Wigner density per unit d^(2n)R; T: ordinary transpose; Omega and hbar: canonical commutator form and scale.
patches.regime: Exact for Gaussian quantum states, not a Gaussian approximation to arbitrary states. The formula integrates to one and reproduces d and V. Singular ideal infinite-squeezing limits are excluded. Nonnegativity of this density is not, on its own, a quantum-physicality test.
patches.units: The denominator is (2 pi)^n because the integration space has 2n real dimensions. W has reciprocal phase-space-volume units. The expression keeps the same form under a consistent quadrature-coordinate change with V and d transformed and W given the density Jacobian. For one mode the vacuum is exp[-(q^2+p^2)]/pi at hbar = 1 and exp[-(q^2+p^2)/2]/(2 pi) in the review's hbar = 2 coordinates.

assumptions: a and a-dagger are a single bosonic mode's annihilation and creation operators, with [a,a-dagger] = 1 and the vacuum defined by a|0> = 0.
theta is real, measured in radians relative to a chosen local-oscillator phase; the displayed phase convention is X_theta = q cos(theta) + p sin(theta).
q = (a + a-dagger)/sqrt(2) and p = (a - a-dagger)/(i sqrt(2)), so [q,p] = i. The displayed 1/sqrt(2) is not the review's unscaled hbar = 2 quadrature convention.

No Gaussian-state assumption is needed for the operator definition. Finite second moments are required only when using its variance; ideal balanced homodyne identifies a calibrated signal proportional to this quadrature, not a complete finite-power/noisy-detector model.
variables: X_theta: Hermitian rotated dimensionless quadrature; X_0 = q and X_(pi/2) = p.
a: bosonic annihilation operator; a-dagger: its adjoint; theta: real relative phase in radians; i: imaginary unit.
q and p: hbar = 1 normalized quadratures; the orthogonal partner is X_(theta + pi/2).
patches.regime: Exact single-mode operator identity, valid for Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. It obeys [X_theta,X_phi] = i sin(phi-theta); hence [X_theta,X_(theta+pi/2)] = i and the vacuum variance is 1/2 at every phase.
patches.units: The card uses dimensionless hbar = 1 quadratures. Write the review's variables as q_W = a + a-dagger and p_W = i(a-dagger-a): q = q_W/sqrt(2), p = p_W/sqrt(2), and X_theta = (q_W cos(theta) + p_W sin(theta))/sqrt(2). Thus the review's unit vacuum variance becomes 1/2 here. In compatible variables with [Q,P] = i hbar, the corresponding quadrature is sqrt(hbar) X_theta.
